reply_text:
I found no dated AI predictions from Yann LeCun in 2019 on any page I could open. I ran all 12 searches (the three fixed ones first) and used all 6 page openings, one of which was blocked.

**What the opened pages held:**
- **VentureBeat, "AI predictions for 2019" (published 2 January 2019):** LeCun gave the interview in December 2018, so it falls under 2018, not 2019. It only describes research goals (self-supervised learning, causal reasoning) with no dates. One line comes close, saying ethics and bias problems "will come," but it gives no date.
- **His ISSCC 2019 paper (February 2019, from his own site):** It makes forward-looking statements about AI, but none has a date or time span. One example: "Future DL systems will largely be trained using a form of self-supervised learning." The few lines with time words are about hardware, such as "In the short and medium term, the bulk of the computation will be convolutions." Hardware forecasts are excluded under your rules.
- **French Morning (3 June 2019, news report of a talk in New York):** LeCun calls Her-style virtual assistants "un futur possible" (a possible future), then adds "Mais ça n'est pas pour demain !" (But that's not for tomorrow!). That has no date and isn't about AGI arriving, so I didn't list it.
- **Lex Fridman Podcast #36 (31 August 2019):** The transcript page only showed the first 17 minutes, and those contain no timeline statement. The rest of the episode is unchecked.
- **Eye on AI interview (19 June 2019):** The page has only a summary, no transcript.

**One lead I couldn't check:** search snippets show an X post by LeCun from about October 2019, correcting how a Les Echos interview reported him. The snippet has him saying he'd be satisfied to build machines with the common sense of a cat or a rat "before the end of my career," and that human-level intelligence will come much later. The page was blocked, so I haven't quoted it or listed it as a candidate. The date is worked out from the post's ID number and the snippet's page age, not read on the page. The post and the original Les Echos interview are the best things to check by hand.

**Not checked:** his October 2019 book *Quand la machine apprend*, the second half of the Fridman episode, and his 2019 Facebook debate with Stuart Russell.
